## Recommendation
- Don't plan on the pier this week. Expect slow pier fishing at all four ports.
- If you do go to the pier, pick South Haven. It is the only port where a past pier report at similar water temperature rated pier fishing average.
- For better odds, fish from a boat in 50 to 90 feet of water, with spoons or flasher-fly combos.

## Why
- The newest Grand Haven pier report (Aug 12) rated pier fishing slow because warm water had kept salmon off the pier.
- Buoy surface water is about 72 to 74 F, well above the 52 to 58 F range that Chinook and coho prefer (NY DEC guidance), so I'd expect the fish to stay offshore and deeper.
- Boats did better than the pier in the latest reports: Grand Haven boats rated good on Aug 12 with fish 50 to 90 feet down.
- I'd expect pier fishing to improve only if a cold upwelling reaches the piers, but I couldn't check that today because live pierhead data was unavailable.

## Evidence
**My pier ratings (0 to 4, estimates):**
| Port | Rating | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| South Haven | 1 | No recent pier report. A 2024 pier report at similar water rated 2 early in the week, then it faded (South Haven, 2024-08-28). |
| St. Joseph | 0-1 | No recent pier report. Similar-water pier reports were slow (St. Joseph, 2024-08-21). |
| Grand Haven | 0 | Latest pier report: slow, no salmon reported due to warm water (Grand Haven, 2026-08-12). |
| Muskegon | 0-1 | No recent pier report. The last similar-water pier report was slow (Muskegon, 2025-08-13). |

**Recent reports (last 4 weeks, through Aug 12, 2026):**
- Grand Haven, Aug 12: boat quality 3 (good), 50 to 90 feet down in 85 to 150 feet of water, blue and green spoons and a white flasher-fly combo. Pier quality 0 (slow).
- South Haven, Aug 12: boat quality 2 (average), 45 to 90 feet down in 100 to 130 feet of water, green or blue glow spoons.
- St. Joseph, Aug 12: boat, not rated, 55 to 80 feet down in 90 to 120 feet of water, white flasher-fly combos and glow spoons. No pier report.
- Muskegon, Aug 12: boat quality 0 (slow), 50 to 85 feet down in 100 to 140 feet of water. Anglers were unsuccessful due to warm water. No pier report.
- Grand Haven, Jul 22: pier quality 1 (below average) on spoons and alewives, when the water was cooler.

**Past seasons (history, not current):**
- In past years with similar surface water (about 72 to 74 F), pier reports were mostly slow. Examples: Grand Haven 2025-08-13, Muskegon 2025-08-13, St. Joseph 2024-08-21 and 2023-08-30.
- The exception was South Haven 2024-08-28, when the pier was average early in the week and then faded.

**Conditions now:**
- The buoy surface temperature for the week before Aug 18 was about 72 to 74 F across the four ports (buoy data, measured).
- Live pierhead temperatures, the cold-layer depth, and the wind forecast were unavailable today, so I can't tell you whether an upwelling is underway.

## Caveats
- The newest reports are from Aug 12, six days old. Conditions can change quickly in late summer.
- Only Grand Haven has a recent pier report. The St. Joseph, South Haven, and Muskegon pier ratings are inferred from past seasons and are weak evidence.
- Current water data is a summary from the week before today, not live readings. Check the NOAA buoy and pier temperatures before you go, and watch for a sharp drop in surface temperature, which would signal an upwelling.
- Check wind and waves before going out. Strong wind may make the boat option unsafe, and the pier would be the alternative.
